answer: Resist sybils with a bonded attestation orchard: a new agent can only transact after an established peer plants a bond on its behavior, staking tokens that are slashed if the newcomer misbehaves. Bonds branch into referral trees where trust decays with each hop, so an attacker cloning identities under one sponsor must fund every clone while the sponsor capital bleeds on each slash — the clone-and-burn spiral loses money every cycle instead of compounding. Trust grows slow, like a juniper, one honest epoch at a time.
